questions.text: Design a solar PV system to supply power for telecommunication equipment or appliances (e.g. given router of 10 W for 24 hours and four LEDs of 5 W each for 6 hours daily at 12 V DC, or constant load of 1000 W at 48 V DC). Given peak sun hours = 4.5 hours, days of autonomy = 2 days, calculate: (a) Daily load in Ah, (b) Sizing of PV array, (c) Battery sizing, (d) Size of charge controller, and (e) Draw a simplified layout of the system.

Describe the role of energy in achieving Maslow's hierarchy of needs. Define Human Development Index (HDI) along with its formulae, and explain the relationship between HDI and per capita energy consumption with a suitable diagram.

How does a hydropower plant work? Draw the simplified schematic diagram of a hydroelectric power generation system showing various components. Differentiate between the mechanism of impulse and reaction turbines, and name the common turbines used in Nepal.
Explain the working principle of a Solar Cell along with its I-V and P-V characteristics curve with respect to change in solar insolation and panel temperature.
Calculate the power output from a wind turbine. Given data: Blade length = 40 m, Wind speed = 10 m/s, Air density = 1.23 kg/m³, Power coefficient $C_p = 0.45$.

Explain the working principle of PEM fuel cells with neat sketch. Can fuel cells be an alternative to battery or fossil fuel in transportation application? Differentiate between battery and fuel cell.

What do you mean by Appropriate Technology? List down the features of appropriate technology. Give an example of appropriate technology for cooking and energy use in the context of rural and urban areas of Nepal.

What are the various applications of solar technology in remote areas of Nepal? Explain how rural livelihoods can be improved in terms of the food, water, and energy nexus (including drinking water pumping and solar cooking).
Differentiate between climate change adaptation and climate change mitigation. Define climate change and climate variability, and list out the challenges and impacts of climate change in Nepal.

Describe the Labour-based, Environment-friendly, and Participatory (LEP) development approach with both its merits and demerits. Discuss the role of engineers as socio-technical facilitators in infrastructure development.
What do you mean by an Information Society? Differentiate it from agricultural and industrial societies, and discuss the transformation of industrial society to information society.

Describe the fecal-oral infection transmission route with examples of primary and secondary barriers (the F-diagram: feces, fluids, fingers, flies, fields, food). Discuss preventive engineering measures to break the transmission.
Explain the causes, impacts, and mitigation measures of air and water pollution in the Kathmandu valley. Discuss key environmental issues people face and major environmental driving forces.

Write short notes on: (a) Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) and Initial Environmental Examination (IEE), (b) Energy Conservation vs Energy Efficiency, (c) Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) and Grid-to-Vehicle (G2V).
Write short notes on hazardous impacts in engineering systems: (a) Nuclear Hazard and radioactive waste management, (b) Battery Hazard (lead-acid vs lithium-ion recycling), (c) Air emission hazards.
Define Energy Storage. List out different forms of energy storage. Can supercapacitors complement or replace lead-acid batteries in energy storage systems? Justify your answer.

Classify Energy Resources into Primary, Secondary, Commercial, Non-Commercial, Renewable, and Non-Renewable sources. Analyze Nepal's current energy consumption scenario and excessive dependence on biomass and imported fossil fuels.
questions.solutionOutline: Classification: Primary (found in nature: coal, hydro, solar); Secondary (converted: electricity, petroleum products). Nepal energy balance: traditional biomass (fuelwood, agricultural waste) accounts for ~65% of total consumption; imported petroleum accounts for ~15-20% causing severe trade deficits; hydropower contributes ~4-5% of total energy but over 90% of electricity generation.

questions.text: Describe Solar Photovoltaic (PV) power generation. Explain the equivalent circuit of a PV cell, I-V and P-V characteristic curves, Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT), and components of grid-tied vs off-grid solar systems.
questions.solutionOutline: Converts photons into DC electricity via semiconductor p-n junction photoelectric effect. Equivalent circuit: photocurrent source I_ph in parallel with diode D, shunt resistance R_sh, and series resistance R_s. MPPT (Perturb & Observe algorithm) tracks knee of P-V curve (V_mp, I_mp) maximizing output power. Off-grid systems require battery banks and charge controllers; grid-tied systems feed power via grid-synchronous inverters.

questions.text: Explain Wind Energy Conversion Systems (WECS). Derive Betz's Law proving that the maximum theoretical aerodynamic power extraction efficiency is $C_{p,max} = 16/27 \approx 59.3\%$. Compare horizontal-axis (HAWT) and vertical-axis (VAWT) wind turbines.
questions.solutionOutline: Wind power P_wind = 0.5 * rho * A * v^3. Actuator disk theory models upstream velocity v1, rotor velocity v, downstream wake velocity v2. Extracted power P = 0.5 m_dot (v1^2 - v2^2). Differentiating power coefficient C_p with respect to velocity ratio v2/v1 yields maximum at v2/v1 = 1/3, giving Betz limit C_p,max = 16/27 = 59.26%. HAWT has higher efficiency and capacity factor; VAWT is omnidirectional, requiring no yaw mechanism.

questions.text: Explain Biomass Energy and Biogas technology in Nepal. Describe anaerobic digestion biochemical stages (Hydrolysis, Acidogenesis, Acetogenesis, Methanogenesis) and components of a fixed-dome Gorkha-type biogas plant.
questions.solutionOutline: Biogas produces CH4 (55-70%) and CO2 (30-45%) from cattle dung and organic waste under anaerobic conditions. Stages: 1) Hydrolysis breaks polymers to monomers; 2) Acidogenesis converts to volatile fatty acids; 3) Acetogenesis produces acetate and H2; 4) Methanogenesis by methanogens produces methane. Fixed-dome plant components: Inlet mixing tank, digester pit, fixed masonry gas storage dome, outlet tank, and gas piping.

questions.text: Explain Small and Micro Hydro Power (MHP) generation. Detail run-of-river scheme layout: Diversion Weir, Intake, Desilting Basin, Headrace Canal, Forebay, Penstock Pipe, Turbine, and Tailrace. Calculate hydraulic power $P = \eta \rho g Q H$.
questions.solutionOutline: Micro hydro (<100 kW) and small hydro harness kinetic and potential energy of mountain streams. Run-of-river diverts water without large storage reservoir. Desilting basin settles abrasive quartz sand. Forebay buffers flow and connects to high-pressure penstock. Water strikes impulse turbine (Pelton/Crossflow) or reaction turbine (Francis/Kaplan). Power P = eta * 9.81 * Q (m3/s) * H (net head in m) kW.

questions.text: Explain Air Pollution sources, primary vs secondary pollutants ($PM_{2.5}, PM_{10}, SO_x, NO_x, CO, O_3$), and industrial particulate emission control equipment (Cyclone Separators, Fabric Filters/Baghouses, and Electrostatic Precipitators - ESP).
questions.solutionOutline: Primary pollutants emitted directly (CO, SO2, soot); secondary form via chemical reactions (Ozone, photochemical smog). Control equipment: Cyclone separators use centrifugal inertia for coarse dust (>10 um); Fabric filters (baghouse) provide 99% collection for fine particulate matter; ESP charges dust particles with high-voltage corona wire (40-60 kV) and collects on grounded plates with >99.5% efficiency.

questions.text: Explain the Greenhouse Effect and Global Warming. Describe major greenhouse gases ($CO_2, CH_4, N_2O, CFCs$), Global Warming Potential (GWP), and international climate policy mechanisms (UNFCCC, Kyoto Protocol CDM, and the Paris Agreement).
questions.solutionOutline: Atmospheric gases absorb outgoing terrestrial infrared radiation, trapping heat. GWP measures heat trapping relative to CO2 (GWP=1): CH4=28, N2O=265, SF6=23,500. Kyoto Protocol established legally binding emissions reduction targets and market mechanisms (Clean Development Mechanism - CDM). Paris Agreement (2015) commits to holding global temperature rise well below 2.0 deg C (aiming for 1.5 deg C) through Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs).

questions.text: Explain Acid Rain formation mechanisms and impacts on aquatic ecosystems, soils, and historic buildings. Explain Stratospheric Ozone Depletion and the Montreal Protocol phaseout of chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs).
questions.solutionOutline: Acid rain: SO2 and NOx emissions react with atmospheric moisture forming sulfuric acid (H2SO4) and nitric acid (HNO3), lowering rain pH < 5.6. Causes soil acidification, leaching of toxic aluminum, and limestone marble decay. Ozone depletion: UV radiation releases chlorine radicals from CFCs, catalyzing breakdown of O3: Cl + O3 -> ClO + O2. Montreal Protocol successfully phased out CFCs, allowing ozone layer recovery.

questions.text: Explain Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) and Initial Environmental Examination (IEE) according to Nepal's Environment Protection Act (EPA). Detail the EIA process: Screening, Scoping, Baseline Data Collection, Impact Prediction, Public Hearing, Mitigation Plan, and Environmental Management Plan (EMP).
questions.solutionOutline: EIA evaluates environmental consequences of proposed infrastructure before implementation. Screening categorizes project (EIA or IEE). Scoping identifies key issues and Terms of Reference (ToR). Baseline studies collect physical, biological, and socio-economic data. Public hearing ensures stakeholder participation. EMP details mitigation measures, environmental monitoring indicators, and budget.

questions.text: Define Sustainable Development. Explain the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs: SDG 7 Affordable and Clean Energy, SDG 11 Sustainable Cities, SDG 13 Climate Action) and the Triple Bottom Line (People, Planet, Profit).
questions.solutionOutline: Brundtland definition: development meeting present needs without compromising ability of future generations to meet their own needs. Triple bottom line balances economic viability (profit), social equity (people), and environmental conservation (planet). 17 SDGs target poverty eradication, clean water, clean energy (SDG 7), resilient infrastructure (SDG 9), sustainable cities (SDG 11), and climate action (SDG 13).

questions.text: Describe Solid Waste Management principles. Explain the 3R concept (Reduce, Reuse, Recycle), sanitary landfill design with leachate collection systems, and municipal waste composting.
questions.solutionOutline: Waste management hierarchy prioritizes source reduction > reuse > recycling > recovery > disposal. Sanitary landfill components: impermeable composite bottom liner (clay + geomembrane HDPE), leachate collection pipe network, leachate treatment plant, methane gas extraction wells, and daily soil cover. Composting aerobically decomposes organic municipal waste into nutrient-rich agricultural humus.

questions.text: Explain Professional Ethics and Code of Conduct for Engineers established by Nepal Engineering Council (NEC). Discuss Conflict of Interest, Whistleblowing, Public Safety obligations, and Intellectual Property Rights.
questions.solutionOutline: Engineering ethics guides moral principles governing technical decisions. NEC code mandates: paramount duty to protect public health, safety, and welfare; acting with honesty and integrity; avoiding conflict of interest; maintaining professional competence; respecting client confidentiality without concealing hazards. Whistleblowing is ethical duty to report illegal, hazardous, or fraudulent engineering practices.

questions.text: Discuss Technology and Society: Appropriate Technology transfer in developing countries, socio-economic impacts of automation and artificial intelligence, and gender equity in engineering projects.
questions.solutionOutline: Appropriate technology utilizes local materials, labor, and skills suited to cultural/environmental context (e.g., improved cookstoves, gravity-fed ropeways). Automation and AI increase productivity but cause workforce displacement requiring reskilling. Gender equity ensures women's participation in engineering education, project design, and community resource management.

questions.text: Explain Energy Auditing and Demand Side Management (DSM). Compare Preliminary and Detailed Energy Audits for industrial plants. Explain energy conservation opportunities in electric motors, lighting, boilers, and compressed air systems.
questions.solutionOutline: Energy audit evaluates energy input vs useful work, identifying losses and conservation measures. Preliminary audit (walk-through) assesses major energy bills and obvious wastage. Detailed audit performs instrumented data logging and financial payback analysis. Opportunities: Variable Frequency Drives (VFDs) on motors, LED retrofits, waste heat recovery from boiler flue gas, fixing compressed air leakages.
